summary: The change implements Iterator.prototype.chunks in its own file, following the spec steps in order. Steps 2-6 are in the right order: the this-object check, the integral check and IteratorClose on TypeError, the range check and IteratorClose on RangeError, then GetIteratorDirect with its `?`. The closure keeps the buffer across resumptions and yields a partial chunk on done. It uses the spec's 1..=2^32-1 bounds with no test-shaped branches. The final flush sets a `flushed` flag so that a return during that Yield is discarded (step 7.b.ii.1.a) and the underlying iterator is not closed. A return during a full-chunk Yield closes the underlying iterator through on_return (IfAbruptCloseIterator). The one lint flag is an unreachable! after an is_integral_number check. It is truly unreachable provided ops::is_integral_number returns true only for Number values, which the spec's IsIntegralNumber requires. I did not see the ops source, so that is an assumption. Nothing is faked and no errors are swallowed.
